images.title: The largest product of 2, 3, 5
images.purpose: Shows that 32 × 5 = 160 beats the runner up 52 × 3 = 156.
images.composition: One large product made of digit tiles in the centre, with the runner up small and grey below it.
images.exact_structure: Centre: three square digit tiles with dark outlines, 3 and 2 side by side as a two digit number, a × sign, then the tile 5 filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with a white numeral, then = 160 in teal #0072B2. The 3 and 2 tiles have white fill. Below, smaller and in construction grey #6B7280: 52 × 3 = 156. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Make the largest digit the multiplier.
images.description: Shows that 32 × 5 = 160 beats the runner up 52 × 3 = 156.
images.context: Picture for finding the largest two digit by one digit product from 2, 3 and 5.

image_decisions.why: The filled tiles with the winning multiplier highlighted show the result the comparison leads to.
